newsitem.title: USA: Quaker says no writeoff for Snapple value.
newsitem.headline: Quaker says no writeoff for Snapple value.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said on Thursday that its Snapple beverage business, which posted an operating loss in 1996, did not qualify for a writedown of goodwill in 1996 under an accounting test.
Analysts had previously expected Quaker to take a large writedown of Snapple, potentially as high as $1.0 billion.

In a teleconference, Quaker Chairman William Smithburg said Snapple was evaluated on the basis of undiscounted cash flow and future prospects for the business. The review was conducted under FAS 121, an accounting standard for asset valuation.
"...Snapple does not qualify (for a writedown) under that test," Smithburg said. "...We'll review the possibility as appropriate in the future."
The chairman reiterated Quaker management's intention to continue to "diligently pursue all options to create value for shareholders," but declined to be specific.
Analysts said Quaker is believed to have been seeking a buyer for Snapple and its Gatorade sports drink business, which is its single largest brand.
"We do not intend to comment on rumors nor do we speculate on possible M&A (merger and acquisition) activity," Smithburg said.
He added that any step Quaker's management and board might take would be "based on value, not speed."
Smithburg said Snapple, which Quaker acquired for a total of about $1.8 billion two years ago, continued to disappoint management in 1996.
"We need to stabilize its volume" in 1997, he added. "Our goal is to operate Snapple at cash positive in 1997."
Cash positive means Snapple is expected to be profitable, adding back goodwill charges of about $50 million a year.
In 1997, Snapple should benefit from a reduction in advertising and merchandising costs, he said.
Quaker said Snapple's sales volume in the United States was down nine percent in the fourth quarter and off 11 percent year-to-date.
Smithburg added that Quaker will introduce a single-serve plastic container for Snapple in March.
Gatorade sales in the United States rose six percent in the fourth quarer and increased four percent year-to-date.
This year, Gatorade will expand with a new "Frost" line of drinks that feature a "cooling taste."
Three flavors in the Frost line began shipping a few weeks ago, Smithburg said. "The trade acceptance has been nothing short of terrific," he added.
